inputs.buildOutcome: Create a complete beginner-friendly Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) Follow Along for a learner starting with no existing infrastructure and no previous Kubernetes experience. Build every required resource from the beginning and never assume that a VPC, subnet, security group, IAM user, IAM role, EKS cluster, node group, kubectl installation, application image or Kubernetes resource already exists. Provide complete separate AWS Management Console and command-line routes, using AWS CLI, eksctl and kubectl where appropriate, and explain clearly which tool each command belongs to. Begin by explaining Kubernetes, containers, clusters, control planes, worker nodes, pods, deployments, replica sets, services, namespaces, labels and desired state in simple language. Walk the learner through creating a dedicated training IAM user and the permissions required for the lab, explain why the root user must not be used, provide every required IAM policy as a properly formatted visible JSON block with a JSON copy button, create and attach the required EKS cluster and node IAM roles, configure AWS CLI access, verify the caller identity and select eu-west-2. Include exact installation and version-verification steps for AWS CLI, kubectl and eksctl, and explain every placeholder before it is used. Walk through creating a purpose-built VPC across at least two Availability Zones with correctly tagged public and private subnets, internet connectivity and any networking required by EKS, then create an EKS cluster named fa-eks-beginner-cluster and a small managed node group named fa-eks-beginner-nodes using cost-conscious training settings. Warn clearly before creating every chargeable resource and explain the expected cost implications without inventing prices. Show how to update kubeconfig, verify the Kubernetes context, inspect cluster and node status, create a dedicated namespace named fa-eks-lab, deploy a simple nginx application using a complete properly formatted YAML block, inspect the deployment, replica set and pods, examine pod descriptions and logs, expose the application first with a ClusterIP service and then with a LoadBalancer service, explain the difference between them, retrieve and test the external endpoint, scale the deployment up and down, perform a rolling image update, inspect rollout status and history, demonstrate a safe rollback, create and consume a ConfigMap, create and consume a non-sensitive demonstration Secret while explaining that real secrets require stronger protection, run a temporary troubleshooting pod, inspect Kubernetes events and resource usage where available, demonstrate pod self-healing by deleting one pod and observing its replacement, and explain how EKS, EC2, Elastic Load Balancing, VPC networking, IAM and CloudWatch work together. Every task must contain however many short separately editable instructions are necessary, exact menu names, buttons, fields, values and commands, explanations of why important settings matter, expected results, visible verification checks, troubleshooting guidance and complete Console and CLI coverage where the operation is supported. Never tell the learner merely to create, configure, record, supply, save or replace something without showing exactly where to click, what to enter and providing the complete required JSON, YAML, policy, command or file content immediately beside that instruction. Use fixed harmless training resource names consistently and define every recorded value before referring to it. Finish with a complete reverse-dependency cleanup stage that deletes only resources created by this Follow Along: remove the Kubernetes LoadBalancer service and verify its AWS load balancer is removed, delete workloads, services, ConfigMaps, Secrets and the namespace, delete the managed node group, delete the EKS cluster, remove the dedicated VPC networking resources in the correct order, detach and delete the created IAM policies and roles, remove the dedicated training IAM user and its credentials where appropriate, and visibly verify that all chargeable resources have been removed. Do not leave placeholder, deferred, future-work, catalogue or incomplete content. Use only official AWS and Kubernetes documentation as factual sources and produce a fully usable beginner walkthrough suitable for AWS and Kubernetes hands-on learning.
